questions.question: In the North-Eastern states of India (Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and Nagaland), primitive slash-and-burn subsistence farming is commonly known as:
questions.explanation: Primitive subsistence farming, commonly known as slash-and-burn cultivation, is practiced on small patches of cleared forest land using primitive tools (hoe, dao, and digging sticks) with family or community labor. In the northeastern states of India—Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and Nagaland—it is traditionally and widely referred to as 'Jhum' or 'Jhumming'. When soil fertility diminishes after a few seasons, farmers abandon the patch and clear a fresh plot, allowing nature to replenish fertility through natural vegetation cycles. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 1.1).

questions.question: Which of the following regional names of slash-and-burn farming in India is correctly matched?
options: Dipa - Bastar district (Chhattisgarh), Podu - Andhra Pradesh, Valre - Rajasthan
questions.explanation: Slash-and-burn agriculture is known by diverse localized vernacular names across the Indian subcontinent: 'Bewar' or 'Dahiya' in Madhya Pradesh; 'Podu' or 'Penda' in Andhra Pradesh; 'Pama Dabi' or 'Koman' in Odisha; 'Kumari' in the Western Ghats; 'Valre' or 'Waltre' in South-Eastern Rajasthan; 'Khil' in the Himalayan belt; 'Kuruwa' in Jharkhand; and 'Dipa' in the Bastar district of Chhattisgarh and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Internationally, it is called 'Milpa' in Mexico and Central America and 'Roca' in Brazil. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 1.1).

questions.question: Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December and harvested in summer from:
questions.explanation: India possesses three distinct cropping seasons: Rabi, Kharif, and Zaid. Rabi crops are winter crops that are sown after the withdrawal of the monsoon rains between October and December. They mature over the cool winter months and are harvested in the early summer between April and June. The success of Rabi crops in northern states (Punjab, Haryana, Western Uttar Pradesh) depends heavily on the availability of precipitation caused by westerly temperate cyclones (western disturbances). (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 1.2).

questions.question: Which of the following groups consists exclusively of Rabi crops?
options: Wheat, barley, peas, gram, and mustard
questions.explanation: Rabi crops are winter-sown crops that require moderate temperatures during germination and vegetative growth, followed by warm, dry sunshine during maturity. The primary Rabi food and oilseed crops grown in India are: Wheat (Triticum), Barley, Green Peas, Gram (chickpea), Mustard, and Rapeseed. In contrast, paddy (rice), maize, jowar, bajra, tur (arhar), moong, urad, cotton, and groundnut are Kharif crops sown with the onset of the southwest monsoon in June-July and harvested in September-October. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 1.2).

questions.question: The success of Rabi crops (especially wheat) in Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh is largely due to winter precipitation brought by:
options: Tropical cyclones from the Bay of Bengal
questions.explanation: In the grain-producing states of northwestern India—notably Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh—the phenomenal agricultural success of winter-sown Rabi crops (especially wheat, barley, gram, and mustard) is heavily reliant on winter precipitation. This vital seasonal rainfall is brought by extra-tropical Mediterranean temperate cyclones, meteorologically termed 'Western Disturbances'. Originating over the Mediterranean Sea and transported across Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan by the subtropical westerly jet stream, these storms provide crucial, life-saving soil moisture that ensures high crop yields and full kernel development before the dry heat of early summer. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 1.2).

questions.question: The short agricultural season between the rabi and kharif seasons during the hot summer months is called Zaid. Which crops are typical of this season?
options: Watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables, and fodder crops
questions.explanation: In between the two major crop cycles—the winter-sown Rabi season and the monsoon-sown Kharif season—there is a short, intensive agricultural season during the hot summer months (March to June) known as the 'Zaid' season. Taking advantage of long daylight hours and high solar radiation, farmers with access to assured canal, tube well, or riverbed irrigation cultivate fast-maturing succulent crops. Key Zaid crops include watermelons, muskmelons, cucumbers, bitter gourds, and leafy summer vegetables, as well as rapid fodder crops for livestock. In addition, sugarcane is an annual crop that spans all three agricultural seasons. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 1.2).

questions.question: Wheat, the primary cereal crop of north and north-western India, requires which environmental conditions?
options: A cool growing season, bright sunshine at the time of ripening, and 50 to 75 cm of annual rainfall evenly distributed
High humidity and frost throughout the year
questions.explanation: Wheat is the second most critical cereal crop in India and the main food staple in north and north-western regions. It is a temperate Rabi crop requiring two essential environmental conditions: (1) a cool growing season with temperatures between 10°C and 15°C during early vegetative growth, and (2) bright, warm sunshine at ripening to harden the grain kernels, accompanied by 50 to 75 cm of evenly distributed annual rainfall throughout the crop cycle. The major wheat-producing belts are the Ganga-Satluj plains and black soil tracts of the Deccan. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 2.1).

questions.question: Ragi, a coarse millet grown extensively in dry red and black soils, is exceptionally rich in which vital nutrients?
options: Iron, calcium, other micro-nutrients, and roughage
questions.explanation: Ragi (Finger Millet) is a hardy coarse grain crop that grows exceptionally well in dry regions on red, black, sandy, loamy, and shallow black soils. Although millets are traditionally categorized as coarse grains, ragi possesses an extraordinarily high nutritional value. It is remarkably rich in dietary calcium, iron, potassium, essential amino acids, and roughage, making it a critical dietary staple for addressing nutritional anemia and mineral deficiencies. Karnataka is the largest producer of ragi, followed by Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 2.2).

questions.question: Why are pulse crops (except Arhar / Tur) customarily grown in crop rotation with other cereals?
options: They are leguminous crops that fix atmospheric nitrogen through root nodule bacteria, naturally restoring soil fertility
They absorb all moisture from surrounding weeds
They grow only when surrounded by wheat
questions.explanation: Pulses (such as gram, tur/arhar, urad, moong, masur, and peas) are the major source of dietary protein in a vegetarian diet. Except for Arhar (pigeon pea/tur), all pulse crops are leguminous plants. They possess symbiotic nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules that capture atmospheric elemental nitrogen and convert it into water-soluble nitrogenous soil nitrates. For this reason, pulses are customarily cultivated in rotational cropping sequences with nutrient-demanding cereals (like rice and wheat) to naturally restore and replenish soil fertility without relying heavily on synthetic chemical fertilizers. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 2.2).

questions.question: Sugarcane is a tropical as well as a subtropical crop. It grows well in hot and humid climates with a temperature of 21°C to 27°C and annual rainfall of:
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is a long-duration tropical and subtropical grass crop cultivated for sugar, gur (jaggery), khandsari, and molasses. It requires a hot, humid climate with a temperature range between 21°C and 27°C and an annual rainfall of 75 cm to 100 cm. In areas with lower rainfall, artificial irrigation is mandatory. Sugarcane can grow on a wide variety of soils from alluvium to black soils, provided they are well-drained. India is the second-largest producer of sugarcane globally, after Brazil. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 2.3).

questions.question: Which oilseed accounts for about half of the major oilseeds produced in India and is a Kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Groundnut is a Kharif oilseed crop that accounts for approximately half (50%) of all major oilseeds produced in India. It thrives in well-drained light sandy loams and red and black soils. In terms of state-level production, Gujarat is the leading producer of groundnut in India, followed by Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh. In southern states, groundnut is also cultivated during the Rabi season under irrigation. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 2.4).

questions.question: The renowned 'Arabica' variety of coffee initially brought from Yemen was first introduced to India on which hills in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Coffee is a major beverage plantation crop in India. The premium 'Arabica' variety of coffee, renowned across international markets for its delicate floral aroma, smooth flavor, and superior cupping quality, was initially smuggled from Yemen in the 17th century by the Sufi saint Baba Budan. The seeds were first planted on the misty slopes of the Baba Budan Giri hills in the Chikkamagaluru district of Karnataka. Today, commercial coffee cultivation in India remains geographically concentrated in the southern Western Ghats, with Karnataka accounting for over 70% of total national output, followed by Kerala and Tamil Nadu. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 2.5).

questions.question: Natural rubber is an equatorial crop requiring which specific environmental conditions for commercial growth?
options: Moist and humid climate with heavy rainfall above 200 cm and temperature above 25°C
Dry arid climate with annual rainfall below 50 cm
Cold mountain climate with severe frost
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is primarily an equatorial plantation crop, but under special agricultural conditions, it is also commercially grown in tropical and subtropical regions. It requires a hot and humid climate with heavy rainfall exceeding 200 cm annually, and temperatures constantly maintained above 25°C. Natural rubber is an essential industrial raw material utilized in vehicle tires, tubes, footwear, and conveyor belts. Kerala is by far the leading producer of natural rubber in India. questions.question: Cotton requires high temperature, light rainfall or irrigation, and how many frost-free days with bright sunshine to mature?
questions.explanation: Cotton is one of the primary fiber crops of India and forms the vital raw material for the cotton textile industry. It grows best in the drier parts of the black cotton soil (regur soil) of the Deccan plateau. Cotton requires high temperatures, light rainfall or canal irrigation, and crucially, at least 210 frost-free days with bright, clear sunshine during its 6 to 8 month maturation phase. Frost is completely fatal to the vegetative development and boll formation of the cotton plant. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 2.6).

questions.question: Jute is popularly known as the 'Golden Fibre'. Why is it losing its market to synthetic alternatives in recent years?
options: Because jute has been banned by the United Nations
Because of its high cost compared to cheap synthetic packing materials like nylon and plastic
Because jute plants have become completely extinct
questions.explanation: Jute, celebrated as the 'Golden Fibre', grows well on well-drained fertile alluvial soils in the floodplains (particularly the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta in West Bengal, Bihar, and Assam). While jute is natural, biodegradable, and strong, it has faced severe market contraction in recent decades because of its high cultivation and processing costs compared to cheap synthetic substitutes (such as nylon and polypropylene bags) and aggressive packaging competition from international producers like Bangladesh. (NCERT Geography Chapter 4, Section 2.6).
